subject: Clarify IP carveouts & runtime usage in MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cobalt-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cobalt-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines: IP allocation + runtime constraints

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement ran a legal review and attached a redline (Cobalt_Redlines_v2.docx) focused on two areas we need clarity on before we can move to signature:

1) Output ownership / title: We need to understand your standard position on customer ownership of outputs created from customer prompts, and whether Redwood reserves any residual rights to use customer outputs for product improvements or model training.
2) Runtime & deployment restrictions: Cobalt wants assurances that models running in dedicated/private modes cannot be used to re-train models outside the scope of the contracted environment. They asked for explicit operational constraints in the Order Form/MSA.

In the doc we proposed short language for an express training opt-out and a narrow telemetry/feedback license for quality improvements only. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the training opt-out and limit any feedback license to aggregate telemetry (no customer prompts or outputs)?

We included a short proposed snippet in proposed-msaoip-snippet.txt (attached) to speed things along. Procurement asked for a 72-hour turnaround if possible.

Appreciate your help — can you loop in legal and let us know the earliest you can respond?

Best,
Oliver
Head of Procurement
Cobalt Analytics

Attachments: Cobalt_Redlines_v2.docx (docx, 58 KB), proposed-msaoip-snippet.txt (txt, 1 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cobalt-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: IP allocation + runtime constraints

Oliver —

Thanks for the redline and the proposed snippet. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (contracts) to review. Quick notes from a GTM/sales perspective:

- We routinely offer a customer opt-out for training on a per-account basis for Enterprise/Private deployments; there are some operational considerations (e.g., inability to use cached prefixes for cross-customer batching) that can affect latency/cost but we can document those tradeoffs.
- We typically accept a narrow telemetry license limited to aggregated telemetry for runtime stability and anomaly detection — not raw prompt/output retention for model training.

Laura — can you review the attached redline and proposed snippet and advise on language we can accept without requiring wholesale MSA edits? If we need a targeted Order Form exhibit or an addendum, flag that and Ben will sketch the procurement path.

Oliver — we should be able to get a legal response within 48–72 hours; Ben can confirm. If procurement needs edits in DocuSign-ready form, let us know.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cobalt-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: IP allocation + runtime constraints

Marissa/Ben/Oliver —

I reviewed Cobalt's redline and the proposed snippet. High-level legal position and suggested compromise below. I'll mirror these into a tracked-change snippet if you want a DocuSign-ready file.

Suggested compromise (summary):
- Output title: Cobalt retains title to Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and prompts. Redwood retains no ownership in customer outputs.
- Training: Customer may elect an opt-out to exclude Customer Content, prompts, and Outputs from use for model training, fine-tuning, or improvement. If Customer opts out, Redwood will implement operational isolation (no persistent storage of prompt/output text for training) and will provide a documented list of telemetry still allowed (performance metrics, error rates, anonymized aggregate token counts).
- Feedback/telemetry license: Rather than a broad feedback license, propose a limited license: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable license to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for service quality, debugging, and to detect abuse; explicit prohibition on using Customer prompts or Outputs for model training or dataset ingestion unless Customer opts in.
- Operational notes: Opt-out may change latency/cost profiles and may preclude participation in cross-customer caching/batching optimizations. We'll include an Exhibit B (Operational Effects of Training Opt-Out) in the Order Form to record these tradeoffs.

Action items:
1) Marissa/Ben: please confirm whether we should push these terms into the MSA core or handle as an Order Form Exhibit. My preference is Exhibit to keep MSA stable and allow per-deal flexibility.
2) Marissa: ask Cobalt if they require an escrow/evidence trail for telemetry deletion; if yes we can propose a quarterly attestation and an ops runbook.
3) Ben: draft a short tracked-change doc for procurement to review; I can sign off on the legal wording.

I'll prepare a tracked-change snippet (DocuSign-ready) and upload it to the HubSpot deal.

—Laura
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-msaoip-snippet.txt (updated, 1.1 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: IP allocation + runtime usage — proposed next steps

Oliver —

Thanks — Laura's language looks like a good path forward. Next steps from procurement/Sales side:

1) I'll convert Laura's summary into a tracked-change Order Form Exhibit (Exhibit B) and attach a DocuSign-ready file to the HubSpot deal by EOD today.
2) Can Cobalt confirm they accept the Exhibit approach (Order Form exhibit vs. MSA amendment)? That will speed execution.
3) On telemetry deletion/attestation: if Cobalt wants an annual attestation that's workable; real-time deletion proofs are operationally heavy. Let us know preferred cadence.

If Cobalt is comfortable with Exhibit + quarterly attestation for deletion/retention metrics, we can get the fully redlined package into DocuSign within 48 hours.

Marissa — I put a short note in the HubSpot deal (link above). Oliver — feel free to call if you want to walk through the Exhibit language live; I can join with Laura.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
